# Live-node commitment fixtures

Captured from an isolated live node on 2026-11-03 using the local GH-566
candidate built from runtime commit
`16823164495a35b0f853d96cf65480eed0393ed6`. The binary was built before that
commit and reports `3e4bc931b20b98e736214f37c7c345a9d9cb24e9+dirty`.
This is candidate-source qualification, not a released-artifact check.
The capture client uses protocol bindings at
`720c855bfb879ed3c1df90d8f71df805da57fd5b`.

| Fixture | hog-devnode | Protocol token | thruput-xdr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bootstrap.hex` | `0.1.2` (local candidate) | `hogp/74deb79e5822565` | Git commit above |
| `hundred-transactions.hex` | `0.1.2` (local candidate) | `hogp/74deb79e5822565` | Git commit above |

Hex is the unmodified XDR `EventIndexerPulledBlock`, read using procedure 10
only and archived from the node's origin by `examples/capture_origin.rs`, which
appends through the same commitment-verifying store as `hog-firehose-store`.

- `bootstrap.hex`: height 1 of a schema-5 bootstrap with a
  faucet and one account (the `thruput-firehose:fixture` account zero);
  one bootstrap transaction, four emitted events.
- `hundred-transactions.hex`: height 32 after 30 empty manual blocks;
  100 signed native-wallet balance calls generated by `examples/submit_traffic.rs`
  with seed `fixture` and nonce start 100000. They commit with no emitted
  events. This is a commitment fixture, not a throughput claim about
  successful contract calls.

The store checks the consensus hash and transaction body hashes only, with
duplicate rejection. No key material is included; accounts use the public local
development seed.

To recapture, select a compatible node and use
`submit_traffic --bootstrap-accounts fixture` to create public allocations.
Start it with `thruput node --bootstrap-accounts FILE`, or pass a schema-5
bootstrap manifest directly to `hog-devnode`. The allocation funds the public
key of `thruput-firehose:fixture` account zero. The node
commits height 1 at startup, before any tailer can attach, and
`hog-firehose-store tail` only bootstraps at the tip, so archive from origin
with `examples/capture_origin.rs` and target height 1 instead. Run
`examples/drive_blocks.rs` until height 31, submit 100 calls with
`examples/submit_traffic.rs`, seed `fixture` and nonce start 100000, drive one
more block and capture again with target height 32. Wrap the
height-1 and height-32 hex at 60 columns without altering its bytes. Confirm
the transaction counts and both roots before replacing fixtures.

A fresh live capture is still the way to refresh fixtures after XDR changes,
never a patch to the old fixture bytes.
